label: SYNTHETIC READER: a test instrument, never a reader. Fictional; not evidence about the book; not readership.
read: RC2 30-page edition, draft PDF, 32 pages, built from dev at 5bde59a3 with the publisher's command (a local copy of the figures list for chapter 1's new Figure line)
first_impression: A confident dark cover with six friendly cast cards, then a book that is lively inside but keeps stopping for dashed 'Figure to come' boxes and half-empty pages.

pages.what_i_see: Dark cover, strong title, six colour-coded cast cards with a one-line mood each, rainbow corner stripe. Breathes well and tells me at once this is a team of characters.
Title page: title, author, subtitle, then a lot of empty white. Plain and unstyled next to the cover, but not cramped.
Contents page holds six lines at the top and the rest is blank. No page numbers beside the entries, so it does not help me jump to a chapter.

Chapter 1 opens well: rule, cast bar, narrator icon heads, good spacing. The 'A slide versus a loop' drawing (speaker, bubbles, A to B arrow) works. But at the foot a dashed 'Figure to come: the player as I saw it on stage' box is printed as text and is cut in half by the page break.

Top of the page carries the second half of the split placeholder (file path text, 'index/talk-site/shots/talk__player.jpg'), so the talk's player UI the words describe is still not shown. Body text then breathes reasonably; the grey quote is easy to tell from narration. Bottom third of the page is empty after the loop section.

The right half of the slide-versus-loop figure (circle of see, ask, see again with tiny factory inside) opens the page; it pairs with page 4 but sits a full page away, so the 'left half, right half' idea is weaker. Text below is comfortable. The 'What a factory is' paragraph runs onto the next page.

Words box is clear and pale. The grey cast-card grid is useful but the right-hand card column is clipped at the page edge ('researcher', 'security' cards touch or cross the margin), and the caption under it is long and small. Page is full: the 'Where this came from' paragraph starts at the foot and splits.
Near-empty page: five lines of source note continued from page 7, then white to the foot. A classic spill page.
Strong page: chapter 2 opener, two Words boxes, dramatised-scene note, and the first agent lines with Dev's two lines under a single head and the mood in italics. Dense but airy enough.

Four lit cast cards with on-stage times work well and the greyed row beneath shows who has not arrived. But the greyed card row is clipped at the right edge, and the narrator and ruv-sgit icons are stacked tightly so the two heads nearly touch. The card text repeats what the dialogue above just said.

A full dashed 'Figure to come: the factory as a chain' box where the Wardley map should be. The text refers to 'look at the bottom row first', so the reader has nothing to look at. Words box and clock section below are readable.

The clock dial with the five steps in the middle is the best picture so far: it shows each member's minute at a glance. Legend and caption are a little small. The reviewer scene starts at the foot and runs over.

The first-wake scorecard and the big '162' work well side by side. Cast bar strip of six lit and three grey heads is a neat image. Page is full but not jammed; speakers (Reviewer, Conductor, Narrator) are easy to tell.

Mostly empty page: a 'Do this now' with one line and a short italic exercise placed tight against the narrator line, then the source note, then white. The exercise is the useful part for me and it is lost in the emptiness.
The stacked bar chart of wakes by hour is clear and shows the empty-chair gap honestly. Good room around it. The reviewer-argument scene starts at the foot.
Two-panel reviewer/researcher card is a readable picture of the dispute; the dialogue is easy to follow with Deck and ruv-sgit in italic moods. The page is full to the foot but not crowded.

Dialogue is easy to follow, but the page is dense and the icons for narrator and ruv-sgit and conductor are small and stacked close, with several short turns in a row. The three 'sent back / held back / owned' cards help me and stay clear of the text.
The afternoon-loop timeline is a good picture. Below it a dashed 'Figure to come: the map of the day' box is printed as text. Text above and below it is fine.
The relayed-word diagram (wall, red cross, direct question arrow) is simple and does explain. Page is full but breathes. A 'Do this now' heading sits near the foot with its text just fitting.
Near-empty page: the end of the exercise (two italic lines) and a 'Where this came from' paragraph, then three quarters white.
Ten-minute dot timeline is a strong picture of the stop, with callouts in the accent colour. Words box and Conductor lines are clear. Page is full; the labels at the top of the dot chart are small.
HOLD file inside the greyed clock, next to the big '82 seconds' card: clear and memorable. Section 'Why stop then' heading sits near the foot with just two lines under it, slightly stranded.

A dashed 'Figure to come: three speech cards' box in the middle. Below it the six-card interview strip is clipped at the right edge (the last card touches the margin) and small text inside cards is hard to read on a phone-sized view.

Dense run of Dev, Narrator, Deck, Storyteller dialogue and a long paragraph, then the 'did not work' cards at the foot. The cards are useful and honest. The text above feels heavy and has little breathing room between turns.

Empty-chair strip works (a dashed empty frame for security is a nice touch) but is clipped at the right edge. The page has strip, long narration, 'Do this now' and a 'Where this came from' paragraph that splits across to the next page.
Near-empty page: four lines of source note spilled from page 25, then white.
Chapter 4 opener. A dashed 'Figure to come: the nine cast cards turning into files' placeholder printed as text. The team's cast list is then given as words with small icons.
Another dashed 'Figure to come: this book's team as cast cards' box, and the page is text heavy with eleven or so speaker turns and a long closing narration. Speaker icons are small.
Two more dashed 'Figure to come' boxes on one page (two cards; three people with a shared brief, board and hold). Content is good but a page with two empty boxes looks unfinished. Page is full.

Opens with a dashed 'Map to come' box where a map is promised. The five numbered step cards are clear, practical and the best page for me as a team member, with 'What to do' and 'What to check' in italics. Page is full to the foot; slightly tight but readable.
Another dashed 'Figure to come: the five steps as a path' box. The cost line, 'Do this now' and 'Zoom in' are fine. Bottom quarter is empty.
Closing 'A book about you doing it' page: a short paragraph and source note, then more than two thirds white. Fine as an ending but feels thin.

speakers_note: One head per run works: Dev on p9, Deck on p10 and Researcher on p16 each show a single name with the mood in italics and later lines hanging under it. The small icons help, but where the narrator and another speaker alternate quickly (p10, p17, p28) the icons are tiny and crowd each other. The narrator's repeated head is the only thing that gets heavy over a long page.
words_on_this_page_boxes: They help. The pale grey-blue boxes (agent, player, repository, commit, hold, check, wake, reviewer, debrief, lock, freeze, session) land just before the word is needed and stay short, so I did not have to flip back. Best on p9 and p11. They sit well against the narrator text and never look like a figure. A few arrive in pairs on one page (p9), which is fine.
top_three_fixes: Replace every dashed 'Figure to come' box (ten of them, p4-5, 11, 18, 23, 27, 28, 29 twice, 30, 31) with the real picture, starting with the talk's player UI in chapter 1 and the Wardley map in chapter 2; never let a placeholder split across a page break.
Stop the horizontal clipping of card rows and strips (p7, 10, 23, 25): keep a right margin so the last card is fully inside the page.
Pull the source notes (and the exercises) back so they do not strand on near-empty pages (p8, 14, 20, 26, 32), and give the contents page entry page numbers.
notes: As a team member preparing a stand, the practical pages (p9-10 arrivals, p12 clock, p21-22 stop and hold, p30 five steps) are what I would hand to the team. The cheeky tone survives onto the page. The marginal clock is hidden as planned and I did not mark it missing.
